description: The plot illustrates how the metric labeled “minFDE\(_{20}\) (←)” varies with the “Number of Examples” for two methods shown as separate lines. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale, and spans integer values from 0 to 8 with ticks at each integer. The y-axis is labeled “minFDE\(_{20}\) (←),” uses a linear scale, and shows values roughly from about 0.205 up to about 0.245 with evenly spaced tick marks (approximately 0.01 apart). One line is blue with circular markers and a solid stroke; it starts near 0.244 at 0 examples, drops sharply to about 0.207 at 1 example, then stays in a narrow band around ~0.206–0.209 through 8 examples, with a low point around 0.206 at 4 examples and ending near 0.207–0.208 at 8 examples. The other line is orange with circular markers and a solid stroke (labeled “Random” in the legend); it starts around 0.232 at 0 examples, decreases to about 0.223 at 1 example, then fluctuates slightly around ~0.222–0.226 across the remaining x-values, with a local low near 0.222 at 6 examples and ending around 0.226 at 8 examples.
